newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ANGRY ROBSON STORMS OUT OF NEWS CONFERENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY ROBSON STORMS OUT OF NEWS CONFERENCE.

text.p: Barcelona coach Bobby Robson stormed out of a news conference on Tuesday after telling reporters he, and not his players, was responsible for picking the team.
"It's a lie, it's a disgrace, and I'm angry with you," said Robson as he walked out.
The former England manager was responding to reports that squad members and club president Jose Luis Nunez were involved in choosing who should play.
"It's not the players, it's not the president, or the doctor, it's nobody but me," said Robson in English, before repeating himself in Spanish for the benefit of the assembled journalists.

Newspaper reports had claimed strikers Hristo Stoichkov and Juan Pizzi had begun warming up without being told to by Robson when Barcelona went 3-0 down to Atletico before their spectacular 5-4 Spanish Cup win last week.
Several Spanish newspapers carried reports on Monday which quoted Robson as thanking Nunez for recommending some changes during the 1-0 league win over Logrones.
Robson's relationship with the press has steadily deteriorated since his arrival at the Camp Nou in the close season.
Problems on the field - Barcelona trail arch-rivals and leaders Real Madrid by nine points - have been aggravated by Robson's limited knowledge of Spanish.
And many journalists are thought to be nostalgic for the era of ex-coach Johan Cruyff, who left Barcelona last May after eight seasons in charge.
Legal action by Cruyff against Nunez for slander began on Tuesday with declarations from witnesses connected to the club.

Nunez accused the Dutchman of accepting money to support rival candidates to the club presidency and of favouring his striker son Jordi over other players in a heated press conference the day after firing the former World Cup star.
